entities.name: Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Known simply as "Rabbi" (the teacher par excellence), Judah ha-Nasi (c. 135–217 CE) was the Patriarch (Nasi) of the Jewish community in Roman Palestine and the redactor of the Mishnah — the monumental codification of Jewish oral law. Descendant of Hillel, he wielded both religious and political authority, maintaining diplomatic relations with Roman emperors (possibly Marcus Aurelius). His decision to commit the Oral Torah to writing was revolutionary — previously it was forbidden to write down oral traditions — driven by the existential threat to Jewish learning after the Bar Kokhba revolt. His Mishnah became the foundation of all subsequent Talmudic literature.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi's codification of the Oral Torah in the Mishnah preserved Jewish learning and identity after the Bar Kokhba revolt, safeguarding a centuries-old tradition for future generations.
